subject: Post-demo alignment — SDK hooks, streaming fallback, and embedding/rerank strategy
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Menon <priya@medicolabs.com>; Sam Ortega <sam.ortega@medicolabs.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo alignment — SDK hooks, streaming fallback, and embedding/rerank strategy

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the candid discussion. Quick written summary from our call and proposed next steps so we have alignment going into the technical POC.

High-level pain points you called out:
- Search and triage latency: current reranker adds ~300–700ms per query and spikes under load.
- Need deterministic structured outputs for downstream EHR ingestion (JSON schema with discrete fields).
- Real-time chat UI requires partial token streaming and safe fallbacks when model latency increases.
- Data residency & PHI handling: logs/audit and key management are blockers for moving to hosted endpoints today.

Goals you gave us:
- 95th percentile L2 response under 600ms in production for triage flows.
- First-pass structured output that maps to the patient-summary schema we reviewed.
- A sandbox environment (dedicated capacity or private deployment) for a two-week POC.

Summary of product fit / recommended approach (what we believe is feasible):
1) Embeddings + rerank: use candidate/embedding hybrid where we precompute doc embeddings (prod infra) and run a lightweight reranker at query time. We recommend a small, quantized reranker variant to hit latency targets. Prefix/KV caching will be configured to reduce repeated token decode.
2) Streaming + function-calling: add streaming responses for the chat UI and wire a function_call surface for your patient-action handlers. For degraded cases we’ll fall back to non-streaming with an explicit compress/shorten policy.
3) Structured outputs: return a top-level JSON blob via function_call (structured output mode) with schema validations. We’ll provide example validators in the Python SDK.
4) Security/compliance: we can provision a private deployment in your GCP VPC or do Redwood Dedicated with KMS-backed keying and restricted audit log retention.

Proposed immediate next steps (timeline):
- Week 0 (this week): share MLP (mutual-action-plan.xlsx) + demo recording (attached).
- Week 1: Redwood engineers spin up a sandbox Dedicated instance and share access; Ben to open tracking Jira (RED-1421).
- Week 2–3: SDK changes (streaming proto + function_call examples) and a small POC that runs the embed->rerank pipeline on a sample dataset.

Who does what (tentative):
- Redwood: Ben (SDK + reranker integration), Karthik (infra + Dedicated sandbox), Ava (PM / acceptance criteria).
- Medico Labs: Priya/Sam to provide representative dataset and the patient-summary JSON schema.

Questions outstanding:
- Which residency option do you prefer (Dedicated in our us-west region vs Private on your GCP)?
- Any contractual constraints on token-level telemetry we should be aware of?
- Preferred cadence for POC syncs (weekly tech deep-dive + weekly business sync?)

Attachments: mutual-action-plan.xlsx, demo-recording.mp4

Thanks — I’ll set up the Jira and share access to the demo. If you’d like a quick follow-up call to lock the sandbox option, I’m free Thursday afternoon PST.

—
Ava Chen
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Priya Menon <priya@medicolabs.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Ortega <sam.ortega@medicolabs.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 13:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo alignment — SDK hooks, streaming fallback, and embedding/rerank strategy

Thanks Ava — helpful summary and clear next steps. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Residency: we prefer Dedicated in your us-west region to avoid the operational burden of managing a Private deployment right now. Can you confirm whether Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS or if Redwood will manage keys?
- Telemetry: we cannot send PHI to Redwood-managed logs. We can send tokenless telemetry or redacted examples for performance debugging. Is token-level redaction supported in the sandbox?
- Cost: do you have a rough order-of-magnitude for the two-week Dedicated sandbox and the POC (GPU hours + SDK engineering effort)? That will help unblock procurement.

Also — we can share a 2,500-record sample dataset by COB Friday. Would that be sufficient for the initial rerank latency tests?

Subject: Re: Post-demo alignment — SDK hooks, streaming fallback, and embedding/rerank strategy

Received — I’ll take SDK ownership for the POC. High-level notes on execution: 

- SDK work: add streaming RPCs to the Python SDK (proto + example notebook), implement function_call wiring that returns a validated JSON object, and include a small validator harness that runs locally against the patient-summary schema. ETA: initial branch in 5 business days.
- Reranker & latency: I’ll prototype a 8-bit quantized reranker variant and a simple prefix-KV cache. If the sample dataset is representative, we should be able to bench to ~350–450ms 95th with Dedicated GPUs (T4s -> 95th might be optimistic; we’ll tune).
- Infra: Karthik, can you confirm Dedicated sandbox provisioning timeline and whether we can enable customer-managed KMS for Medico? I’ll link RED-1421 here and add tasks for SDK + benching.

Linking internal items: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RED-1421

Thanks — I’ll post updates to the Jira and ping Priya when sandbox is up.

—
